label: Get the Job — Advisory Pricing & Proposals
overview: The advisory pricing and proposal templates give the advisor a professional, defensible way to scope, price, and present advisory engagements. Three core tools cover the full spectrum: the Advisory Pricing Model for complex or team-based engagements, the General Advisory Proposal for bespoke consulting, and the Lite Fundamentals Proposal for foundational coaching programs. The Variation to Scope of Works document protects the advisor against scope creep once the engagement is underway.

diagnostic_entry.primary_question: What type of engagement are you pricing — is it a bespoke, custom consulting job, a foundational coaching program, a due diligence review, or has the client requested something outside the original scope?

materials.name: Advisory Pricing Model
materials.summary: A spreadsheet that takes the guesswork out of pricing — bundled options, content suggestions and a Blank Team matrix that lets fees be built from the actual people assigned to each task. It breaks a complex job into scoping, research, presentation and implementation, and includes a detailed Due Diligence Scoping Model for mergers and acquisitions. For the owner it makes the fee transparent; for the firm it protects profitability and stops scope creep.
materials.who_when: Firms putting several team members on one project, and complex bespoke engagements — especially due diligence or structural reviews.
steps: Hold the discovery session first and understand what the client actually needs before any number is written down.
Enter your staff names and their travel, prep and advisory rates into the Blank Team Pricing Matrix tab — this has to be done before the calculation sheets will work.
Break the project into its components: Introduction, Scoping, Research, Presentation, Implementation, Review.
Assign the appropriate team member to each task and allocate the hours against them.
Keep the chargeable line clear — discovery, scoping and research analysis may be charged; presenting the proposal generally is not.

For a merger or acquisition, use the Due Diligence Scoping Model inside the same spreadsheet to price structural, asset and staff review tasks such as asset utilisation, staff contracts and supplier risk.

materials.name: General Advisory Proposal
materials.summary: A slide deck that turns discovery findings into a logical pitch, visually connecting the client's End Game to the actions needed to reach it. It names their objectives and the Legitimate Constraints holding them back, and — unusually — states how many hours of the client's own time the work will demand, so expectations are set from day one rather than argued about later.
materials.who_when: Clients needing bespoke, customised consulting built around their own specific business problems.
steps: Open the proposal once the pricing model has mapped the bespoke tasks.
List the client's business objectives in their own terms.
List the Legitimate Constraints — what is genuinely holding them back today.
In Recommendations, detail the steps to win, and state the hours the CLIENT or their staff must commit; those hours are theirs, not the advisor's.
Present the monthly investment and the total fee together, so the commitment is clear in both forms.

materials.name: Lite Fundamentals Proposal
materials.summary: A pre-campaigned, out-of-the-box advisory programme built on three digestible pillars — Getting More Organised, Getting More Work, and Doing More Profitable Work. It demystifies growth by teaching fundamentals such as the working capital cycle, the four levels of consumer awareness and process improvement cycles, and it is generated from a merge table rather than written from scratch, which makes it scalable across many clients.
materials.who_when: Smaller businesses and clients who need foundational coaching and structured systems rather than a complex customised intervention.
steps: Confirm the client needs foundational help — general business education, better systems, or basic marketing and sales planning — rather than bespoke consulting.
Open the merge table tool in the advisor portal.
Enter the client's data into the tool and let it populate the proposal fields automatically.
Pitch the three pillars in order: Getting More Organised, Getting More Work, Doing More Profitable Work.
Present the monthly investment and total fee as with any other proposal.

materials.name: Variation to Scope of Works
materials.summary: The document that keeps a signed engagement honest when the client asks for something that was never quoted — financing new equipment, a bank finance application, any new project appearing after the agreement. It records the new issue, the timeline and the additional fee, and is signed before the extra work starts rather than invoiced afterwards.
materials.who_when: Any signed engagement where the client raises an out-of-scope request — used immediately, not at the end.
steps: Recognise the request as out of scope the moment it arrives, rather than absorbing it.
Open the Variation to Scope of Works document included at the end of both proposal templates.
Document the newly identified issue or opportunity in plain terms.
State the timeline and the additional estimated fee — for example 14 hours at $3,700.
Obtain the client's signature before commencing any of the extra work.

advisor_guidance.chargeability: Discovery, scoping, and research are generally chargeable. Proposal presentation is generally not — but for highly complex engagements, the scoping meeting itself may warrant a charge.
advisor_guidance.scope_creep: The most common profitability leak in advisory work is scope creep. Use the Variation to Scope of Works document every single time without exception — not just for large requests.
advisor_guidance.proposal_choice: Bespoke client with unique problems: General Advisory Proposal. Smaller client needing foundational coaching: Lite Fundamentals Proposal. Merger or acquisition: Advisory Pricing Model with the Due Diligence Scoping tab.
